title: Detection on shifted compact generators
statement: Let C be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with Type v indexed coproducts and morphism universe v. Let I : Type v and E : I → C consist of compact objects [def-pc-compact-object] whose coproduct weakly generates C [def-pc-generators]. Let H : C opposite → Ab be cohomological [def-sp-homological-functor; def-sp-abelian] and preserve all Type v indexed products. For any G : C and any natural transformation α : Hom_C(-,G) → H, if α on E(i)[n] is an isomorphism for every i and integer n, its component at every object is an isomorphism. The map and object are inputs, not constructed here.

proof.text: For the given α define P(Y) to mean invertibility of α on Y[n] for every integer n. Shift composition and naturality give closure under shifts and isomorphisms. Apply the cohomological long exact sequences for representable Hom and H to a distinguished triangle and its shifts. The naturality squares commute, so the five lemma gives P for the third object when it holds for the other two.

Both H and the represented Hom functor take coproducts to products. Shift equivalences preserve coproducts; under the product comparison α on a coproduct is the product of its components. Products of isomorphisms are isomorphisms, so P is closed under coproducts. Applied to a telescope triangle, coproduct closure and triangle closure give P for its homotopy colimit whenever all stages satisfy P.

The generator hypothesis on α says P(E i). The compactGenerators_buildObjects theorem expresses an arbitrary Y as a telescope with initial object a coproduct of shifts of E and transition cones also such coproducts. Thus the initial object has P; induction using its transition distinguished triangles shows every stage has P. Telescope closure gives P(Y). Taking shift zero and transporting along the canonical shift-zero isomorphism gives invertibility at op Y, hence at every object of C opposite.
